messages:
Ava Nguyen: Quick sync — I'm proposing we route customer outbound traffic through regional perimeter egress connectors (one per-region) instead of spinning per-tenant connectors. Pros: fewer ENIs, lower NAT/GW costs, simpler monitoring. Cons: breaks per-tenant source IP preservation, harder to give tenant-specific egress policies.
Miguel Ortiz: +1 to fewer ENIs, huge cost upside. How do we feel about IP preservation? Some customers (payments) require static egress IPs.
Priya Shah: For those customers we can offer a reserved per-tenant NAT as a premium (Dedicated). But defaults should be regional for scale.
Sam Blake: Operational question: with regional connectors, do we still keep the control plane peered into tenant VPCs or move to PrivateLink endpoints? We need minimal access for handshake/cert rotation.
Ava Nguyen: Idea: keep control plane separation — maintain a lightweight one-way peering for agent bootstrap only, then use regional egress for data path. Handshake tokens + short-lived certs handled over bootstrap.
Miguel Ortiz: Concern: one-way peering still adds cross-account routes and route table complexity. Could we instead use an ephemeral bootstrap connection from agent to control plane via a customer-initiated PrivateLink proxy? Less route churn.
Priya Shah: PrivateLink avoids route proliferation but adds per-tenant ENIs on our side (N LB target). Might be similar cost. Also complicates RBAC and audit trails.
Sam Blake: We also need to consider failover. If a region perimeter connector goes down, traffic should failover to another region or to a fallback per-tenant connector.
Ava Nguyen: Rollout plan I'm thinking: 1) Opt-in beta customers. 2) Canary traffic with header tag X-Redwood-Egress: regional. 3) Observe NAT session counts, Conn tracking, and cold-start latency for new flows.
Priya Shah: Measurement hooks we need: per-tenant active flows, source IP mapping table size, KV caching hit rate for prefix caching, and error spike when fallback triggers.
Miguel Ortiz: Small config snippet for canary header check in proxy:
```
match:
  - header: X-Redwood-Egress
    value: regional
route: regional-perimeter
```
Sam Blake: Deployment question: how do we perform cert rotation for agent control plane when peering is minimized? Can we push rotation over the API over the PrivateLink during maintenance window?
Ava Nguyen: Yes — rotations can be initiated from control plane to agent using the existing bootstrap channel. If PrivateLink isn't available, agents will fetch rotation tokens from S3 signed URLs (short-lived) — we already have that flow for air-gapped installs.
deploy-bot: deploy-check: canary-connector v2 passed smoke tests in us-west-2 :white_check_mark:
Miguel Ortiz: Security note — ensure ACLs on regional egress connectors prevent lateral tenant access; treat them as shared infrastructure with strict SNAT table per-tenant records.
Priya Shah: Ops playbook snippet: If regional egress overloaded -> 1) increase connector replicas -> 2) throttle non-critical tenants -> 3) promote reserved per-tenant NATs for top customers.
Sam Blake: Agree. Also add an automated alert when SNAT table occupancy > 75% for more than 5m.
Ava Nguyen: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with rollout risk matrix and canary gating metrics. Volunteers for review: @Miguel, @Priya, @Sam? :pray:
Miguel Ortiz: I'll review today.
Priya Shah: On it.
Sam Blake: I'll take reliability and playbook sections.
Ava Nguyen: Thanks — filing RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. Closing thread unless anyone objects.
